title: Three Polarizers
intro: The packet now carries a polarization (the colour in the polarization view: red = horizontal, cyan = vertical). It leaves horizontal, and a vertical polarizer guards the target: crossed polarizers pass nothing. A polarizer at angle θ passes cos²(θ − θ_in) of what reaches it and leaves it polarized along θ, so adding polarizers can let more through. Place them between the source and the guard and set their axes (drag the dial handle). Order matters.
goal: Place up to two polarizers between the source and the vertical guard and set their axes with the dial, so the packet gets through to the target.

physics.point: A polarizer keeps only the part along its axis and leaves it polarized along that axis. Crossed polarizers block everything, but polarizers in between let light through.

idea: Polarization is a direction carried by the wave. This packet starts horizontal (0°). A polarizer at angle θ lets it through with probability cos²(θ − θ<sub>in</sub>) and absorbs the rest. Whatever passes is now polarized along θ.
The guard is vertical (90°), crossed with the start: cos²90° = 0, so nothing gets through.

Put a polarizer at 45° in front of it. Half passes, now at 45°, and half of that passes the guard. A filter that only removes light has made more light arrive, because it changes the polarization of what it lets through.
For a single particle cos² is a probability. Each polarizer is a measurement that asks 'along θ or across?', and a 'yes' resets the state to θ.
maths: Malus's law, applied once per polarizer:

maths.eq: P = cos²θ₁ · cos²(θ₂ − θ₁) · cos²(90° − θ₂)

maths: With two polarizers the best is three equal 30° steps:
One at 45°: (cos²45°)² = 0.25. Reversed order, 60° then 30°: cos²60° · cos²30° · cos²60° ≈ 0.047.

Even with nothing in the way the target catches only about 55% of the packet, so P<sub>T</sub> is about 0.55 times these: measured 22.9% (30°, 60°), 13.5% (45°), 2.7% (reversed) and 0.03% with no polarizers.
With N equal steps the loss vanishes as N grows: cos²ᴺ(90°/N) → 1. Level 6-2 builds on this.
try: Place one polarizer at 45°: P<sub>T</sub> ≈ 13%. Add the second and set the two to 30° and 60°: P<sub>T</sub> ≈ 23%.
Swap their axes so 60° comes first: P<sub>T</sub> drops to about 3%. Order matters.
Set a lone polarizer to 0° or 90°: it passes everything or nothing, and the guard still blocks.
